answer: The posted-speed model is too fast almost everywhere: it underpredicts the observed 2025 structural-fire median travel time in all 167 scored ZIP areas (n>=20), mean bias -2.2 min, RMSE 2.3, only 5 within 1 min, r=0.48. Worst: 11101 Long Island City (model 1.5 vs observed 5.1 min, -3.6), 10018 (-3.6), 11360 Bayside (-3.5), 10007 (-3.5), 10038 (-3.5), 10001/10118 (-3.3), 10036 (-3.2), 10021 (-3.2). Midtown/Lower Manhattan, western Queens and the Bronx are worst. Likely causes (not tested here): no traffic, signals, turns or acceleration at posted speed; actual first unit often not the nearest house (busy or multiple units); street midpoints weighted equally, not fire locations; model starts at the firehouse door. Observed range is compressed (2.5-5.9 min vs model 0.8-3.8). Best fits: 11210, 10035, 11239 (~-0.7 to -0.9).
traps_or_caveats: Observed field is incident_travel_tm_seconds_qy (travel, not response incl. turnout); valid_incident_rspns_time_indc='Y'; structural fires 2025 only.
Postal ZIPs mapped to MODZCTA via member lists; unmatched reported not dropped: 11249 (94 incidents), 10151 and 10178 (1 each), blank zip (110). 11249 is therefore missing from the comparison.

Because error is one-sided (all negative), the 'most wrong' ranking is mostly a ranking of how much the uniform bias is exceeded; after removing the -2.2 bias, outliers are 11210 and 10035 (over-fit by ~1.6) and 11101/10018 (under by ~1.4).

Causes are hypotheses; traffic, dispatch-from-other-house and incident location were not measured. Observed ZIP values merge postal-ZIP medians weighted by incidents (approximation); model is the median of street-segment midpoints (rw_type 1), not incident-weighted.

Model assumes posted speed with no delays; 540 street points beyond 15-min cutoff or unsnapped (e.g. 36 in 10018, 66 in 10035) are left out of the model median. Firehouse list has 219 located sites; engines may not all be staffed/nearest.
